lessons: Drain pause must not return EXIT_OK. Keep the session open while paused: loop on `await pause.allow_offer()` through the injected clock/seam until the matching hold-bound release arrives, then continue with the same ticket/offer. Call `_draw_retry` only after the release.

tests/test_drain.py must also prove the release half of criterion 2. While paused, publish a release bound to `pause.hold_id` (e.g. from a scripted seam/clock hook). Assert: no draw or transition before the release, then exactly one dispatch, and exactly one retry draw in the parked case.

Decision-before-mutation needs a direct probe. Wrap `DispatchPause._apply` (or the hold mutation) so it reads `journal.read()` at mutation time, and assert the `control/<request_id>` 'accepted' decision is already present. Checking the journal only afterwards passes even when the order is wrong.

The daemon side passed review: ControlInbox hold supersession via `discard_hold`, latest-wins, stale lifecycle, and dormancy. Keep that design. Rework only the drain wait loop and the missing test proofs, all inside the fence.
reason: Review found three fixable defects, all inside the fence: the drain exits on pause instead of holding, the drain release proof is missing, and there is no direct decision-before-mutation probe. The findings name each fix, so a same-capability retry should resolve them.
